title: Routing & Quotas: edgecase weekly log and action board
content:
Week of 2027-06-14: quick notes from the routing/quota weekly sync. This doc collects the weirdness we saw in QA + a short action board. Meant to be a lightweight, shareable ledger between control-plane, routing, auth and SRE rotations.

Attendees:
- Avery Chen (note-taker)
- Marcus Patel (routing lead)
- Sasha Rodriguez (auth/quotas)
- Diego Morales (SRE)
- Lina Gupta (release-eng)

High-level summary:
- Three recurrent failures surfaced during burst test: 1) quota window miscount on multi-tenant routes, 2) routing fallback thrash when preferred region saturated, 3) token-auth cache expiry not aligned with quota refresh. These are low-rate in prod but reproducible in stress harness.

What we observed (repro steps / signals):
- Quota miscount: When a tenant uses parallel requests across 3 routes that share a parent quota, the parent window occasionally double-counts one request. Repro: run loadgen with 12 concurrent streams across routes A/B/C (see PLAT-1423). Metrics: parent_quota.count jumped by +2 for a single request in ~0.3% of runs. Logs show two increment events within 3ms.
- Routing thrash: During regional saturation, smart-router attempted 2x fallback then reverted back leading to extra external hops. Root cause looks like race between capacity heartbeat and fallback circuit window. Observed increased p99 latency and higher error budget burn.
- Auth cache expiry drift: KVS entries for auth tokens expire at 59s but quota refresh rounds at 60s; small clock skew in the kv-store client makes tokens momentarily invalid and triggers a full auth revalidate which resets quotas in certain codepaths.

Immediate mitigations (done):
- Flip a short-lived toggle to disable smart-router aggressive fallback in canary (Marcus) — reduced thrash in canary by ~40%.
- Added a short-term debounce in quota increment path to dedupe near-duplicate increment events (Diego) — deploy in canary at 2027-06-16 11:30 PT.
- Adjusted auth client to use server-timestamp when available to avoid client-side skew misrounding (Sasha) — hotfix rolled to staging.

Open action items (owner / ETA):
- PLAT-1423: Investigate race in parent-quota increment path; add a TTL-backed operation id to increments and ensure idempotency in the parent counter (owner: Avery Chen) / ETA: 2027-06-25.
- PLAT-1489: Smart-router fallback state machine audit; proposal to add a short cool-down window and commit to a single fallback per request (owner: Marcus Patel) / ETA: 2027-06-30.
- PLAT-1501: Evaluate switching quota increments to event-sourced log + reconciler to avoid transient double-counts (owner: Sasha Rodriguez) / ETA: spike complete 2027-06-22.
- Infra task: Add a 'time-drift-monitor' to SRE dashboards to alert >50ms drift between quota service and auth service clocks (owner: Diego Morales) / ETA: 2027-06-20.

Design notes and options we debated:
- Option A: Make parent quota increments fully transactional by routing through a single leader. Pro: simple correctness. Con: single point of bottleneck for high-throughput tenants.
- Option B: Keep distributed increments but make them idempotent using operation-ids and background reconciliation. Pro: scales better, easier to roll out incrementally. Con: adds reconciler complexity and eventual consistency window.
- Option C: Rethink quota semantics: move from increment-on-request to credit-based leasing for bursty tenants; more complex and may require billing changes.

Decisions made:
- Short term: implement idempotency tokens on increments + debounce to reduce observed duplicates (we can ship quickly and roll back).
- Long term: run spike for event-sourced reconciler (PLAT-1501) and sizing impact on dedicated routing pools.

Risks and unknowns:
- Reconciler approach will change accounting semantics for edge-case billing; finance needs to be looped in if reconciliation can cause retroactive adjustments.
- Leader-based parent increment simplifies correctness but will require sharding rules to avoid hotspot.

Notes to followups / blockers:
- Need a small test harness that can deterministicly produce the double-count with instrumentation — current loadgen sees flakiness; Lina to pair with Marcus to iterate on harness (blocking PLAT-1423 repro).
- Terraform change to enable cool-down toggle in canary vs prod (release-eng dependent).

Quick links and references used in the meeting:
- PLAT-1423 (jira): parent quota double-count reproducible notes
- PLAT-1489 (jira): smart-router fallback state audit
- PLAT-1501 (jira): quota reconciler spike
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/278 (debounce increment patch)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Quota+Edge+Cases+Gallery

Next sync: 2027-06-23, same time. Please update your tickets with any new findings, and flag anything that looks like a billing impact so we can loop finance early.

Notes to self / scratch:
- Try toggling the kv-store client to prefer server time earlier in the stack (less downstream surprises).
- Consider instrumenting operation-id generation path to include route shard id (makes dedupe cheaper).

End of notes.
